name: Stereo width without Haas: microshift, split EQ, humanize doubles
goal: Widen synth/pad layers without relying on Haas: (1) tonal microshift—duplicate, hard-pan L/R, fine-detune one side a few cents (keep under roughly ±5–10 cents); (2) complementary/split EQ on hard-panned duplicates; (3) MIDI-humanize a doubled part (timing/velocity) then hard-pan L/R; keep sub/bass mono-safe (~<100–150 Hz).

source.title: 3 Ways To Widen Your Mix - Without The Haas Effect

prerequisites: Duplicate tracks or dual oscillators; EQ; MIDI humanize/transform or manual velocity/timing tweaks; correlation meter helpful

inputs.name: mono_bass_hz
inputs.description: Keep below this freq mono-safe (~100–150 Hz)

outputs.name: wide_layer
outputs.description: Widened pad/keys layer with healthier mono than heavy Haas

steps.action: First use ordinary panning for width. Only then apply advanced widening. Prefer non-Haas methods to protect mono compatibility.

Tonal microshift: duplicate the part, hard-pan L and R, fine-tune one side by a few cents (transcript examples around −5 to −10; avoid large intervals). Works in synth osc detune or on bounced audio with polyphonic pitch.
Split/complementary EQ: duplicate, hard-pan L/R, change EQ shapes differently on each side (or mid/side bands) so L and R spectra disagree—creates width. Dial gently in context.
Humanize double: duplicate MIDI, randomize/humanize timing and velocity slightly on one copy, hard-pan L/R—simulates a second played take.
Protect low end: keep roughly under 100–150 Hz mono/tight (safe-bass / mono-maker on widened groups). Watch correlation so phase does not collapse.

verification: At least one non-Haas technique applied (microshift, split EQ, or humanize double)
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Delta vs odd/even unison and chord-split skills: uses detune cents, complementary EQ, or performance humanize—not voice-count parity or interleaved chord muting.
Avoid stacking Haas across many tracks; these methods are the preferred alternatives from the transcript.
